content.text: The text combines a celebration of orchards and gardening with historical notes, indexes, footnotes, and Dutch colonial instructions for Jaffnapatam. It praises gardens for pleasing every sense, discusses horticulturists, flowers, orchards, bees, planting, and landscape design, and records figures such as Pope, Bacon, Milton, Switzer, and Evelyn. Zwaardecroon’s memoir details Jaffna’s administration, taxation, trade, forts, roads, water tanks, elephants, pearl fisheries, horse breeding, slavery, churches, and military stations; Governor de Heere adds corrective orders. A later fictional narrative follows Eli, who enters Arne’s room and garden, then walks with him to the parsonage; they later travel to her wedding at Boeen. In another adventure, Sam, Jimmie, Carl, and Pedro shelter inside a temple while Indians besiege it. Mr. Havens works from a hotel, sends Ben to the airfield for telegrams, returns to his hotel suite, and eventually sends the aeroplanes southward.
